site.name: Cherenkov
site.tagline: Interactive olympiad editorials for informatics, physics, and astronomy — every proof paired with a visualization you can actually manipulate.

home.heroBody: Each editorial is written by someone competing in that subject, not teaching it from the outside. Instagram carries the hook — the surprising idea, in a few seconds. This site carries the rest: the full proof, and an interactive visualization you can actually manipulate rather than just read.

about.title: About
about.philosophyPlaceholder: Neutrino observatories never see a neutrino directly — it passes through ordinary matter almost every time. What gets detected is the flash of light the neutrino leaves behind on the rare occasion it does interact, and that flash is enough to trace it back to where it came from. That's the idea behind this project. The reasoning that cracks a hard problem is usually invisible — easy to read past without noticing it was ever there. The visualization is the flash: the moment that reasoning becomes something you can see and trace for yourself.
about.repoBody: Cherenkov is built in the open. Every editorial is a git-tracked file — see the commit history and contribute on GitHub.

footer.madeBy: A public-repo project by the Cherenkov team.
